newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end at low since Sept 1992.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end at low since Sept 1992.

text.p: Sustained foreign selling sent the Thai stock market to close Monday at its lowest level since September 1992.

The SET Index finished retreating 26.41 points, or 3.35 percent, at 761.63. The SET 50 Index ended at its all time low of 55.92, down 2.52 points or 4.31 percent. Turnover was a meagre 2.06 billion baht.
Investors were worried the bourse would carry the impact of a steadily weakening baht against the dollar despite a relatively stable baht/dollar on Monday, traders said.
"Foreigners were concerned about the baht again. There seems to be growing concensus offshore particularly from New York," said a broker at National Finance.
The energy sector lost 6.44 percent, finance 6.30 percent and property 4.98 percent. Late buying helped pare losses in the afternoon when the index fell to an intraday low of 754.07.

"It was all pretty much foreign selling today and the locals were mostly sidelined to watch development. I think there is still some pressure to come because of currency rumours," said a local broker.
A rare Thai balance of payments deficit in December that was announced last week has triggered a round of attacks on the baht in currency markets.

Italian-Thai fell the daily limit low shedding 13 baht to 118, and Siam Cement was off 60 to 740. Reports of reduced gas and crude oil reserves hurt PTTEP which hit another limit low, declining 36 baht to 334.
Fragile sentiment is likely to remain on Tuesday on currency concerns, and worries surrounding payment on a maturing ECD issue by troubled developer Somprasong, analysts said.
